text: Emory Andrew Tate III, born on 1 December 1986 at the Walter Reed Army Medical Center in Washington, D.C., is an American and British social media personality, businessman, and former professional kickboxer who gained notoriety for promoting controversial positions within the manosphere. He has been described as the "king of toxic masculinity," has called himself a misogynist, and is politically categorized as both right-wing and far-right. As of June 2025, he has 10.7 million followers on Twitter and was the third-most googled person in 2023. He is multiracial, with an African American father, Emory Tate (1958–2015), a chess international master, and a White English mother, Eileen Tate, who worked as a catering assistant. He has a younger brother, Tristan, and a younger sister, Janine. Raised in Chicago, Illinois, and Goshen, Indiana, he moved to Luton in Bedfordshire, England, in 1997 after his parents divorced, living on Marsh Farm, which he described as the "worst area of the worst town." He was educated at Halyard High School and Luton Sixth Form College. Tate began practising boxing and martial arts in 2005 and worked in television advertising. From 2005, he began his kickboxing career in England, winning several titles, including the English ISKA Full Contact Cruiserweight Championship in 2009 and the International Kickboxing Federation Full Contact Cruiserweight British Title, and earned the nickname "King Cobra." In 2011, he won his first ISKA full contact world title in a rematch against Jean-Luc Benoît via knockout at 81.5 kg. He competed in the Enfusion 3: Trial of the Gladiators tournament in 2011 and 2012, winning a semi-final match but losing in the final. In 2013, he won his second ISKA world title in the Light Cruiserweight division. He held the Enfusion 90 kg world title in 2014 and became a four-time kickboxing world champion, retiring in 2014 due to eye injuries sustained during his career, which required surgical repair and led to a permanent retirement by age 30. In 2020, he returned to kickboxing, winning knockouts over Miralem Ahmeti, Iulian Strugariu, and Cosmin Lingurar in Romania, before retiring again with a 76–9–1 record. His brother Tristan, who also competed in kickboxing, retired early with a 43–9 record due to a shoulder injury. In 2016, Tate appeared on Big Brother's 17th series as a member of "The Others," but was removed after six days due to an ongoing police investigation into him for rape, which was later dropped. In December 2022, Tate and his brother were arrested in Romania with two women, and in June 2023, all four were charged with rape, human trafficking, and forming an organised crime group to sexually exploit women. Accusers reportedly went into hiding after a campaign of online harassment, and the Tate brothers filed a $5 million defamation lawsuit. In March 2024, British police obtained an arrest warrant for the brothers. In July 2024, a civil case in the UK was brought against the brothers and a third person for alleged tax evasion. In August 2024, Romanian police raided four properties owned by Tate and expanded the investigation to include trafficking minors, sex with a minor, money laundering, and attempting to influence witnesses. Tate and his brother have denied all charges. In May 2025, the UK Crown Prosecution Service brought multiple charges against Tate and his brother Tristan, including rape, actual bodily harm, and human trafficking. Tate and his brother launched a webcam business employing up to 75 models, selling "fake sob stories" to male callers, which they later admitted was a "total scam." They operated Hustler's University, a platform where members paid $49.99 monthly for courses on wealth accumulation and male–female interactions, including cryptocurrency, copywriting, and e-commerce, with an affiliate marketing program that was later shut down by Stripe and criticized as a pyramid scheme. The platform was rebranded as The Real World, which targets male teenagers and features a "cult-like atmosphere," with members referring to each other as "G" and Tate as "Top G," centered on his "41 Tenets for men." The Real World also offers cryptocurrency, e-commerce, and drop shipping. In 2023, Google and Apple removed The Real World's app, the Real World Portal, from their app stores. In January 2024, analysis found the Real World YouTube channel had 450 million views and a third-party channel had nearly 300 million views, with researchers estimating YouTube earned up to £2.4 million from ads, though YouTube disputed the figures. In May 2024, a misconfigured database leaked personal data of 968,447 users, including email addresses and passwords, and 22 million messages. In November 2024, a cyberattack exposed 794,000 usernames, 324,382 email addresses, and the contents of 221 public and 395 private chat servers. The War Room, advertised at $8,000, promotes self-discipline, confidence, and personal responsibility, claiming to teach men physical, mental, emotional, spiritual, and financial development. According to a BBC investigation, the group is an all-male, secretive society with a leader, Miles Sonkin (Iggy Semmelweiss), who met Tate in 2018 and established the group in 2019. Leaked chat logs revealed a "Pimpin' Hoes Degree" course (abbreviated to PhD) that taught techniques to "romantically seduce, emotionally manipulate, and socially isolate women" before luring them into webcam work, described by a human trafficking expert as using "Lover Boy" strategies. Victims reported that sex was used as a manipulation technique and that members engaged in "Pavlovian conditioning," including submission tests like receiving tattoos of members' initials. A whistleblower claimed to have been "brainwashed" by the group. As of August 2022, the group had 434 members and 45 potential victims. In 2024, Tate launched a meme coin called DADDY, which reached a market capitalisation of $217 million, a play on Iggy Azalea's $MOTHER coin, with Tate stating it was "for the patriarchy" and saying, "We're bringing the Gs back, make me a f***ing sandwich females." As of March 2025, Tate is facing six legal investigations—four criminal and two civil—in Romania, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

Andrew Tate is an influencer in the manosphere and "alpha male" community, described as right-wing and far-right, and identified as a libertarian; he is dubbed the "king of toxic masculinity." He has been criticized for promoting views that women "belong in the home," "can't drive," and are "given to the man and belong to the man" as "a man's property," and for claiming men prefer dating 18- to 19-year-old women to "make an imprint" on them, labeling women who do not stay home as "hoes." In 2017, Tate expressed views on sexual harassment that suggested victims share responsibility for assaults and supported Russell Brand after allegations of sexual assault. He is associated with far-right ideologies and individuals, including Tommy Robinson, and has appeared on InfoWars and with figures like Mike Cernovich, Jack Posobiec, and Paul Joseph Watson; he attended CPAC in 2019. Hope not Hate has accused Tate of a "long history of racist statements, homophobia and links to the organised far-right," and Thierry Baudet called him an "outspoken political dissident." Tate has questioned whether the Nazis were the "bad guy" in WWII, performed Nazi salutes, and advocated bringing the Nazi salute back, responding to Elon Musk's salute in January 2025 by saying, "we're so back." In a 2023 BBC interview, Tate claimed he was "acting under the instruction of God" and preached hard work, discipline, anti-drugs, religion, no alcohol, and no knife crime. He has stated that depression "isn't real" and named conspiracy theorist Alex Jones a hero; in March 2024, he falsely claimed the Francis Scott Key bridge collapse was due to a cyber-attack. Tate was accused of inciting online hate after amplifying misinformation about the Southport stabbing, leading to far-right riots in the UK. Regarding the Gaza war, he accused Israel of "genociding" Palestinians and said the October 7 attacks were "an eye for an eye," and stated, "I can only pray for a death as heroic as Yahya Sinwar." He promoted an antisemitic conspiracy claiming the "Matrix" is the Jewish mafia and said, "stop crying over the Hitler crap" and questioned whether lies about WWII were also told about Gaza. Beginning in 2022, Tate's influence on teenage boys and young men has raised concerns among parents, teachers, and mental health experts globally, including in North America, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand. The New York Times described his views as "brainwashing a generation," and the Anti-Defamation League (ADL) considers his misogyny mainstream, stating he teaches that women are inferior and morally deficient and deserve physical, sexual, and emotional abuse, equating his philosophy to pickup artists. The White Ribbon Campaign called his commentary "extremely misogynistic" and its effects on young males "concerning," while Hope not Hate warned his content presents a "dangerous slip road into the far-right" and criticized his ties to far-right groups. Rape Crisis England and Wales said it is "unacceptable" that such misogyny is given a platform, and the Centre for Countering Digital Hate labeled his videos "extreme misogyny" for referencing leaving an imprint on young women. In response, Tate claimed his content includes "many videos praising women" and aims to teach audiences to avoid "toxic and low-value people," saying he plays a "comedic character" and that people believe "absolutely false narratives" about him. Tim Squirrell of the Institute for Strategic Dialogue said Tate poses a risk of radicalising young men into misogynist extremism, and Hope not Hate's director of policy called him a "legitimising force" for misogynistic views, while the End Violence Against Women Coalition said it is "hugely concerning" that he continues to influence younger men who agree with his views on women, masculinity, and how to be a man. Teachers in Australia reported a rise in sexism, misogyny, and sexual harassment in classrooms, with some quitting their jobs. In February 2023, teacher training courses on addressing Tate's views sold out. The UK's head of counter-terror policing expressed concern about the effect of such rhetoric on young boys, and the Department for Education discouraged discussion of Tate due to his influence on sexual harassment and misogyny. The Australian government allocated AUD$3.5 million (£1.8 million) to counter harmful gender stereotypes online, responding to young fans bringing misogynist views into schools. In February 2024, the UK shadow education secretary, Bridget Phillipson, proposed peer-to-peer mentoring programs to counter Tate's misogyny, a plan welcomed by the National Education Union. A 2023 survey by "The Man Cave" found 28% of 500 teenage Australian boys looked up to Tate and 36% found him relatable, with half of 24 schools reporting a significant negative impact. A Hope not Hate survey found 80% of British males aged 16–17 had viewed Tate's content, with 45% of those aged 16–24 having a positive view compared to 1% of British females aged 16–17. YouGov data in September 2023 found 26% of men aged 18–29 and 28% of men aged 30–39 agreed with Tate's views on women, with 6% of adults who had heard of him holding a positive view (12% men, 3% women) and half having a negative view. A 2023 Women's Aid and ORB International survey found 40% of 7–18 year-olds had heard of Tate, including 21% of 7–11 year-olds and 43–53% of 11–18 year-olds, with children exposed to his content being five times more likely to think hurting people is OK. A 2024 King's College London, Center for Women's Global Leadership, and Ipsos study found one in five men aged 16–29 who had heard of Tate held a favourable view (7% of women in the same age group), with only 6% overall holding a favourable view and over three-quarters holding an unfavourable view; one in seven agreed with his views on male identity and gender roles, while 61% disagreed. Tate's early YouTube channel, "the Hateful Tates," gained attention, and by July 2022, he was searched more than both Donald Trump and COVID-19. In August 2022, TikTok videos of Tate were viewed 11.6 billion times. By December 2023, he had over 8.5 million followers on X (Twitter), an increase of 5 million since December 2022, and as of August 2024, had 9.9 million followers. He was the third-most googled person in 2023, and his Wikipedia article was among the top 25 English Wikipedia articles in 2023. In December 2022, Tate tweeted to environmentalist Greta Thunberg, boasting about his 33 cars, including a Bugatti with a w16 8.0L quad turbo and two Ferrari 812 competizione models with 6.5L v12s, and requested her email to share details of his car collection and emissions. Thunberg responded with the satirical email "smalldickenergy@getalife.com," which went viral. Tate gained notoriety for promoting a "hyper-masculine, ultra-luxurious lifestyle" and "hyper-macho image," and is popular among British teenage boys who mimic his phrases and philosophies. Virtually every parent in Britain had heard of him, and parents and teachers expressed concern about his influence leading to misogynistic and aggressive behavior. In January 2023, the BBC reported that Tate and his brother used social media to contact young women to join their webcam business. The Center for Countering Digital Hate found YouTube earned up to £2.4 million from Tate's content, accusing YouTube of turning a blind eye; YouTube disputed the figure as "wildly inaccurate and overinflated." Three of Tate's Twitter accounts have been suspended, with one account created to evade a ban being verified by Twitter before being permanently banned. In August 2022, after an online campaign to deplatform him, Tate was permanently banned from Facebook and Instagram, losing 4.7 million followers, and Meta cited violations of policies on "dangerous organizations and individuals." TikTok removed his account for violating policies on content that attacks, threatens, incites violence against, or dehumanises individuals or groups. Shortly after, YouTube suspended his channel, which had 760,000 subscribers, citing hate speech and COVID-19 misinformation, and Tate later deleted his Twitch channel.

Three of Andrew and Tristan Tate’s Twitter accounts have been suspended at different times. In 2021, an account created by Tate to evade a prior ban was verified by Twitter, contrary to its policies, and was later permanently banned, with Twitter stating the verification occurred in error. In August 2022, after an online campaign to deplatform him, Tate was permanently banned from Facebook and Instagram, losing 4.7 million followers from the latter; Meta cited violations of its policy on "dangerous organizations and individuals." TikTok removed his account after determining it violated policies on content that attacks, threatens, incites violence against, or dehumanises an individual or group, with videos featuring Tate’s name as a hashtag receiving over 13 billion views. YouTube suspended his channel, which had 760,000 subscribers, citing multiple violations, including hate speech and COVID-19 misinformation, and Tate later deleted his Twitch channel, which had 50,000 subscribers. In November 2022, after Elon Musk acquired Twitter, Tate’s Twitter account was reinstated. Tate responded by stating that while most of his comments were taken out of context, he took responsibility for how they were received. Jake Paul denounced Tate’s sexism but called the bans censorship. Tate’s content continues to circulate on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok via fan accounts. After the bans, Tate moved to alt-tech platforms Gettr and Rumble, causing Rumble to briefly become the most downloaded app on the Apple App Store. In 2025, Tate stated he launched the BRUV (Britain Restoring Underlying Values) Party as part of his plan to become prime minister, with the party’s website declaring it a "war to reclaim Britain" to defend borders, crush crime, purge corruption, and restore national pride. The party launch was widely ridiculed, with one user calling its manifesto a "mix of North Korea and homoeroticism" and another calling it the "very worst idea in the history of British politics"; some speculated it was a PR stunt, but Tate dismissed it, stating he was "100% serious" and would run in the next election. The party’s Twitter handle was suspended but was restored after Tate made a complaint to Elon Musk. In 2017, Tate and his brother moved from the UK to Romania, where they run multiple businesses; Tate cited a preference for countries where corruption is accessible and claimed he would face fewer rape charges there, noting that Romanian police require "evidence" or "CCTV proof" for rape reports, unlike the Western world during the #MeToo movement. He reportedly has several children in Romania whom he visits occasionally. Tate was raised Christian but later became an atheist; by early 2022, he identified as Christian again, tithing £16,000 monthly to the Romanian Orthodox Church. After a viral video of him praying at a mosque in Dubai in October 2022, he announced on Gettr that he had converted to Islam; scholars such as Mufti Menk have commended the decision, calling him a "very sincere brother." In March 2023, during incarceration in Romania, Tate’s legal team reported a "dark spot on his lung, most likely a tumor" following a Dubai medical consultation, sparking online rumors about lung cancer; Tate denied having cancer on Twitter. In June 2025, it was revealed Tate received Vanuatu citizenship through the country’s citizenship by investment scheme in December 2022; a Vanuatu government spokesperson stated they were "definitely looking into" revoking his citizenship. Tate was first arrested in Britain in July 2015 after two women accused him of rape and assault, and was arrested again in December 2015; in 2019, the Crown Prosecution Service declined to file charges. Canadian alt-right activist Lauren Southern wrote in her 2025 memoir that she met Tate in Romania in 2018; she described being taken from a nightclub to her hotel room, kissing him briefly, and then being strangled unconscious after resisting his advances, stating she would prefer not to share the rest. In April 2022, the US embassy received a report that an American citizen was being held against her will in a property owned by the Tate brothers in Pipera, Romania; Romanian police raided the home and a nearby webcam studio, discovering four women, two of whom (the American and a Romanian woman) claimed they were held against their will, triggering an investigation by DIICOT into human trafficking and rape. In December, the Tates and two women were arrested; all four were suspected of human trafficking and forming an organised crime group, with one suspected of rape; Romanian authorities seized 29 assets, including cars, properties, watches, and money, totaling nearly US$4 million. In June 2023, DIICOT upgraded the charges to "human trafficking in continued form," a more serious charge, with seven victims identified; the four accused were indicted on charges of rape, human trafficking, and forming an organised crime group to sexually exploit women; they deny all charges and remain under investigation for money laundering and trafficking of minors. In the same month, the Tate brothers filed a defamation lawsuit against one accuser, their parents, and two others in Palm Beach County, Florida, seeking $5 million in damages, claiming the five conspired to falsely accuse them. In January 2024, the Romanian criminal case was heard in the preliminary chamber, and three months later, the Bucharest Tribunal ruled that the case met legal criteria. That month, US District Judge Robin L. Rosenberg dismissed another defamation lawsuit by the Tates against a former US Marine who reported them to the US Embassy and military officials. In March 2024, Westminster Magistrates' Court issued a European arrest warrant against Andrew and Tristan Tate, based on allegations of sexual aggression from 2012 to 2015; the brothers categorically reject all charges. In July, Devon and Cornwall Police began civil proceedings against Tate, Tristan, and a third person for tax evasion with their online businesses; two months later, three women involved in the British investigation and a fourth British woman filed a civil case against Tate. In August 2024, Romanian police expanded their investigation to include trafficking minors, sex with a minor, money laundering, and attempting to influence witnesses; prosecutors said the new investigation involves 35 alleged victims, including a woman who was a minor at the time; the Tate brothers, among six detained, denied all allegations. In December 2024, the Westminster Magistrates' Court ruled in favor of Devon and Cornwall Police, allowing them to seize £2.8 million in unpaid taxes from the Tate brothers’ online businesses. In February 2025, Alison Hernandez, Police and Crime Commissioner for Devon and Cornwall, announced the force received around £1.2 million, which she intended to support victims of violence against women and girls. In the US, following pressure from the Trump administration on Romanian authorities to lift travel restrictions, Tate left Romania by private jet and arrived in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, where he became the subject of a statewide criminal investigation. In March 2025, Florida’s Attorney General, James Uthmeier, initiated a criminal investigation into Tate upon his arrival. Tate’s ex-girlfriend, Brianna Stern, accused him of choking and beating her at The Beverly Hills Hotel on 10 March, claiming she was later diagnosed with post-concussion syndrome; she filed a lawsuit against him for physical and sexual abuse. Tate denies the accusations. In May 2025, the UK Crown Prosecution Service brought 21 charges against Tate and his brother Tristan, including rape, actual bodily harm, and human trafficking.
